From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the Seller's framing does not bind us

- **"[STANDARD]", "cleared by both sides", "FINAL", "settled at principal level".** These are the Seller's own labels. Nothing in our authority process confirms them. Under playbook §0.4/6.3 every item below has been reviewed on its merits.
- **"Market standard" claims** (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month limits) are assertions, not verified facts. They do not move our positions.
- **No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for any fallback.** Where a Seller number happens to match a fallback (20% cap, 18 months), that does not clear it.
- **The Disclosure Letter contradicts the cover note in several places.** It confirms that Bluefen consent is not delivered, Riverlark is not repaid, and the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow. Below I rely on those disclosed facts rather than the cover note's characterisations.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable (cl. 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject all three elements.
- **Reason:** Five times our thresholds plus an excess-only basket would shield a large volume of genuine loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl. 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep.
- **Reasons:**
  - 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval, which has not been given.
  - The sweep would silently impose the short period on Title, Tax, fraud and the indemnities.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title to the shares is the core of what we are buying. Capping it at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative point.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps and baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy; and
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express carve-out. This point is non-waivable.
- **Reason:** "All Claims of any nature" would purport to limit fraud claims, and the playbook prohibits anyone waiving this.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1–1.2. Accept only the specific disclosures in DL 2–10, each against identified warranties.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure is expressly rejected by our playbook. The cover note's claim that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework" is unverified and incorrect.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. If any qualifier survives:
  - it must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; and
  - it must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete.
- **Reason:** Combined with general disclosure, it would gut the warranties, including on matters the Seller has itself disclosed (e.g., Ironquay, DD-006).

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl. 3/6.3).
- **Facts:** DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen represents ~AUD 3.6m, about 30% of revenue.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - effective consent as a Completion condition; and
  - evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient for a customer worth about 30% of revenue.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7).
- **Facts:** DL 3 confirms approximately AUD 3.2m is outstanding, the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge. The facility has change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - executed security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval. Neither is in place, and the debt-free price basis requires payout at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs either:
  - included as a specific funds-flow line item / deduction; or
  - expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion.
- **Reason:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion, so the liability lands on the Company, which we will own.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is "adequate" (cl. 11.1).
- **Facts:** DL 4 records the following:
  - transfer of SOW3 materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl. 7.3);
  - AUD 180,000 is recorded open in DD-010, which is not bank-verified;
  - there is no payment receipt; and
  - there is no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - the indemnity broadened to cover all loss from any failure of IP to vest, and third-party claims;
  - the SOW3 cure preserved (payment plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally pre-Completion); and
  - the AUD 180,000 treated as unverified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form.
- **Reason:** The risk is defective IP ownership, not just an unpaid invoice.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch 6).
- **Facts:** DL 6 records a link to ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - regular updates before Completion; and
  - no materiality characterisation baked in.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" language. Add investigation and information covenants, and consider a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Neither side can yet say whether there is a breach, harm or notification duty. Our position should not assume one either way, and should not adopt the Seller's conclusion.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Facts:** DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on terms, timing and related-party aspects before classifying them.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation. Request the documents and assess.
- **Reason:** This is unresolved either way. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction from us, and no ordinary-course label from them.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Several provisions fold every category into the general regime:
  - the "applies to all Claims" limitations;
  - the "all Claims of any nature" exclusive remedy and non-reliance; and
  - Title and Tax/IP placed under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each governed by their own express terms, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject, and redraft with express category carve-outs.
- **Reason:** These sweeps are hidden overrides that would undercut N-004, N-005, N-011 and N-016.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 itself concedes the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of:
  - title;
  - share issue history;
  - absence of encumbrances (e.g., a PPSR search, and Riverlark security discharge per N-009); and
  - Seller authority.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.
- **Reason:** The register is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof of title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both treated as OPEN, with no deemed resolution in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" assertion and keep both open for negotiation.
- **Reason:** No resolution has been agreed through our process. Our position should not assume unlimited liability, and should not accept the Seller's subordination of these items to a 20% / 18-month regime.

---

## Summary for the deal team

- **Rejected or kept open:** All 16 items. No point is acceptable as drafted.
- **Priority items:**
  - **N-005 (fraud):** non-waivable.
  - **N-004 / N-014:** Title and category separation.
  - **N-006 / N-007:** the disclosure plus knowledge combination.
  - **N-008 / N-009:** Bluefen and Riverlark, both pre-Completion deliverables.
  - **N-010:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs.
- **Fallbacks:** None are deployable on the cap (N-001) or time limit (N-003) unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
- **Seller's covering positions:** We should respond in writing that we do not accept the "[STANDARD]/cleared/FINAL" designations or the claim that the disclosure and limitation framework has been accepted.
